name_note: GTDB divides Phocaeicola plebeius into lineages and marks this one _A; papers and NCBI use the undivided name Phocaeicola plebeius (formerly Bacteroides plebeius).

sentences.text: Phocaeicola plebeius is a species of the Bacteroidetes phylum found in human faeces.
A study of 52 healthy and 144 liver cirrhosis individuals reported it significantly reduced in abundance and identified it as a microbial biomarker for cirrhosis.
In the same work, treating a mouse model with P. plebeius improved cirrhosis-related phenotypical and biochemical markers and lowered expression of several fibrosis-related genes.
A study of children with new-onset untreated epilepsy reported depletion of Phocaeicola plebeius relative to controls.
Among people living with HIV, a study reported Phocaeicola plebeius enriched in individuals with a smaller intact viral reservoir.
